calendar_source: Odia Kohinoor / Radharamana Panji & Odisha Gazette

festivals.name: Veer Surendra Sai Jayanti
festivals.significance: Birth anniversary of the iconic Odia freedom fighter.

festivals.name: Basanta Panchami (Saraswati Puja)
festivals.significance: Worship of the Goddess of learning; initiation of Akshaya Tritiya chariot wood collection.

festivals.name: Maha Shivaratri (Jagara)
festivals.significance: Night-long fasting culminating in the raising of the Mahadipa at Lingaraj and Puri temples.

festivals.name: Dola Purnima
festivals.significance: Grand swing festival of Radha-Krishna deities; reading of the new solar almanac.

festivals.name: Utkal Divas (Odisha Day)
festivals.significance: Commemorates the foundation day of Odisha as a separate linguistic province in 1936.

festivals.name: Maha Bishuba Sankranti / Pana Sankranti
festivals.significance: Traditional Odia Solar New Year. Offering of sweet 'Bela Pana' to Tulsi plants.

festivals.name: Akshaya Tritiya
festivals.significance: Commencement of the construction of Ratha Yatra chariots and the Akhi Muthi Anukula farming ritual.

festivals.name: Savitri Amavasya
festivals.significance: Fasting observed by married Odia women for the well-being and longevity of husbands.

festivals.name: Pahili Raja
festivals.significance: First day of the three-day agrarian festival celebrating swing games, Pitha, and earth fertility.

festivals.name: Raja Sankranti
festivals.significance: The peak day of Raja Parba, where no farming operations take place to let the earth rest.

festivals.name: Devasnan Purnima (Snana Yatra)
festivals.significance: Ceremonial public bathing of Lord Jagannath's Trinity, leading to the 15-day Anasara isolation.

festivals.name: Puri Ratha Yatra (Sri Gundicha Yatra)
festivals.significance: The world-renowned Chariot Festival journey from Srimandir to the Gundicha Temple.

festivals.name: Bahuda Yatra
festivals.significance: The grand return chariot leg of the deities back to the Singhadwara of Jagannath Temple.

festivals.name: Gamha Purnima (Raksha Bandhan)
festivals.significance: Worship of cattle alongside standard Rakhi rituals, honoring the birthday of Lord Balabhadra.

festivals.name: Nuakhai
festivals.significance: The massive harvest festival of Western Odisha where communities consume the first grains of new rice.

festivals.name: Kumar Purnima / Gajalaxmi Puja Begins
festivals.significance: Autumn full-moon evening worship by youth; kicks off the massive Gajalaxmi festivals.

festivals.name: Anla Navami
festivals.significance: Amla tree worship and the holy 'Radha Pada Darshan' at the historic Sakshigopal Temple.

festivals.name: Kartika Purnima / Boita Bandana
festivals.significance: Floating of toy paper/bark boats at dawn to honor Kalinga's historic trans-oceanic maritime trade.

festivals.name: Prathamastami
festivals.significance: Honoring the first-born child of the house with new garments and steaming of Enduri Pitha.
